name: Saint Lucy
history: A young Christian of Syracuse in Sicily who gave her dowry to the poor and was martyred under Diocletian. Her name means light, and her feast, near the darkest days of the year, is kept with candles, especially in Scandinavia. She is named in the Roman Canon.
meditation: Be a light in someone's darkness today.
life: Lucy was martyred at Syracuse in Sicily in the persecution under Diocletian, around 304, and an inscription from about 400 shows that her feast was already kept there. The details of her story come from later Acts. They tell that she was a young Christian of wealthy family who had resolved to give her life to God. Her mother, Eutychia, was ill, and the two went on pilgrimage to the tomb of Saint Agatha at Catania, where her mother was healed. Lucy then persuaded her to give the dowry to the poor. The man she had been promised to denounced her as a Christian. The governor ordered her taken to a place of shame, but tradition says she could not be moved, and she was killed by the sword. Later tradition linked her with the eyes, and she is the patron of the blind.
prayerTo: Saint Lucy, your name means light, and you gave away all you had for Christ. Pray for the blind and for all who live in darkness of body or soul. Keep the eyes of my heart clear, that I may see what God asks of me, and help me to be a small light for others in these dark days. Amen.
penance: Light a candle in prayer today for someone going through a dark time, and give to a charity for the blind or partially sighted.
prayer: Graciously hear us, O God of our salvation; that as we rejoice in the festivity of blessed Luciæ Vírginis tuæ, we may be instructed in the affections of a loving devotion. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
